items.description: The `ArgoCDTools` repo exists with the presync entrypoint, its support code and the Dockerfile — and it is a working repo of this estate: its own `.kubecoder/project.yaml` with `jenkins: IaC/ArgoCDTools`, whose lint and test verbs are green from the repo root.

items.area: R1 — the flow: clone at SHA
items.description: The entrypoint clones the deploy repo at exactly the SHA it was handed, and that is the run's only clone. The clone authenticates via an inline credential helper, never a token-in-URL remote.

items.area: R1 — the flow: the state backend
items.description: The entrypoint starts terraform-backend-git on localhost inside its own process space, waits for it to accept, and points Terraform at it through `-backend-config` address/lock_address/unlock_address at init — pointed at the same state repo and keying as `iac`. The state key is `argocd/<repo>/<stage>/terraform.tfstate`.

items.area: R1 — the flow: terraform init/apply with the stage tfvars
items.description: `terraform init && terraform apply` runs in the clone's `terraform/`, and every `config/<stage>/*.tfvars` in the clone reaches that apply — the tfvars come off the hook's own disk and never travel through Argo (D14).

The entrypoint synthesises a kubeconfig from the pod's own ServiceAccount and exports both `KUBE_CONFIG_PATH` and `KUBECONFIG` at it before `terraform init`, so a bare `provider "kubernetes" {}` configures itself from that file. The proof asserts the synthesis and its selection over any ambient kubeconfig — a result that would also hold via this pod's `~/.kube/config` proves nothing.

The reattach finds `Released` PVs whose `claimRef` names the run's target namespace and nulls `claimRef.uid`/`resourceVersion`, leaving PVs outside that namespace untouched. The namespace is the fourth Job argument, used as given — the hook derives it from nothing. Exercised against a deliberately-`Released` PV on the prd cluster (the operator's 2026-08-14 amendment), inside the throwaway `presync-proof` fixture the ruling scopes — two namespaces and hostPath PVs the proof creates and deletes, with no PV outside the fixture touched. The fixture's cluster-scoped objects are created over SSH (`sudo microk8s kubectl` on `srvk8s1`, per `docs/live-infra-access.md`), because the mounted `~/.kube/config-prd-write` is namespaced-edit only and can create neither a PV nor a namespace.
The entrypoint exits non-zero when any step of the flow fails and zero only when the apply succeeded — proven on both paths, including a deliberate failure, so a swallowed failure could not pass.

A real entrypoint run from this pod exercises clone-at-SHA → backend → `init`/`apply` → exit code against a throwaway deploy repo and a scratch state key, on both the success and the deliberate-failure path. No Argo CD, no `argocd-hooks` namespace and no OpenBao credentials are needed for it — the run sets the environment variables directly.

The Dockerfile bakes exactly what the job needs to run and nothing general-purpose — the four D31 names plus the distro `python3` the entrypoint runs under, `librados2`/`librbd1` for the cgo `pvginkel/homelab` binary, the Terraform CLI config routing that provider to the estate's mirror, and the step-ca root the mirror's chain needs — and nothing is cloned at runtime except the deploy repo. Terraform is unpinned from the hashicorp `noble` suite and terraform-backend-git is pinned to v0.1.11, as `iac` does both. `support/iac-image/` and the `iac` image are untouched.
CI publishes `registry:5000/argocd-hook:<n>` — a push to `ArgoCDTools` triggers `IaC/ArgoCDTools`, the build succeeds, and the numbered tag is in the registry.

items.area: R2 — the default pin lands in the library chart
items.description: The library chart's values carry the default hook image pin and it names the actual first `IaC/ArgoCDTools` build — the two repos' first releases coordinated, per the inherited ruling that 007 owns confirming or correcting the number.

The entrypoint's argument contract and the library chart's Job template agree on four arguments — repo, revision, stage, namespace — each `required`-guarded in the template, so a chart that forgets one fails to render rather than passing an empty argument, and in that order, since the entrypoint takes them positionally. The guard and the order assertion are shown to bite, not assumed to.

`homelab-shared` publishes as 0.2.0: the version bumped, the new tarball committed to `dist/`, the already-published 0.1.0 tarball unmodified in tree and history, and the repo's own publish and render gates green.

The hook's credentials are its own, minted deliberately, and delivered as plain environment variables: the container knows nothing about OpenBao, AppRoles or any credential provider. **No AppRole is minted** — no hvac, no `!bao` resolver, no secrets manifest in the image. Configuration arrives the same way: `ArgoCDTools` commits no estate facts — no copy of `clusters.yaml`, no Ceph mon host, S3 endpoint, `zfs_pools` map or age recipient anywhere in the repo — and a value the run needs but did not get fails the run by name rather than reaching Terraform as an empty string.

The inventory is complete against the estate's Terraform capabilities and settled to the key name: every key the container reads, the OpenBao leaf and property behind each secret, and — for the non-secret per-cluster facts the same ExternalSecret carries as `template` literals — the `clusters.yaml` value each one is copied from. It is what slice 009 authors the ExternalSecret from, so the names are unambiguous and nothing the run needs is missing from the one object that composes its environment.
The git token's required permissions are stated precisely enough for the operator to mint it: state repo read-write, deploy repos read-only, plus `admin:repo_hook` per D39/D41.

The state encryption key is `iac`'s existing age keypair, readable by the prd `eso` AppRole — one keypair in one leaf, so no rotation can leave state that one side of the same state repo cannot decrypt. The private half is fetched from that leaf and the public half is a `template` literal, so the leaf is written to by nobody and the operator's handover carries no conditional. The Ansible change granting the read is the only OpenBao policy change the slice makes; every other leaf in the inventory is already covered.

The operator writes the secret values: the slice hands over the exact `bao` commands, the paths and the PAT permissions, and no agent runs `ansible-playbook`, writes an OpenBao value, or mints a token.

Nothing in slice 009's half is built here: no `argocd-hooks` namespace, no `tf-presync` ServiceAccount or RBAC, no ExternalSecret, no ApplicationSet parameter. And nothing touches `support/iac-image/`, srviac's `iac-agent` AppRole or its `/etc/iac/secrets.yaml`.

items.area: The cross-slice export — the four-argument contract in the documents
items.description: The `argo-cd` document set states the four-argument contract everywhere it stated three, so a planner reading only that set builds slice 009's ApplicationSet with four parameters: design.md's flow step, its Job skeleton, the sentence naming the arguments and the ApplicationSet `parameters:` block, with the namespace carrying the same `<app>-<stage>` expression the set already computes for `destination.namespace`; and D29/D33 say the reattach's namespace is passed rather than derived. Written as if it had always been true — no supersession notices in the register.

items.area: The cross-slice export — the credential model in the documents
items.description: The `argo-cd` set states the enumerated-leaves credential model wherever it named the dedicated AppRole: phases.md A.2's own credential line, D33's list of what ESO provisions, and D41's account of what bounds a hook run. D41's blast radius is stated as what it now is — exactly the enumerated provider credentials, not a KV prefix spanning every app — and says that it is tighter than what it replaced. The set also says that the same Secret carries the run's non-secret per-cluster configuration, so a planner authoring the ExternalSecret from it and from this slice's inventory produces the whole of what a run receives.

items.area: The root cause — the doc plan names the set
items.description: `slice-doc-plan.md` carries the `argo-cd` document set as a surface, distinguished from the homelab `decisions.md` it is easily confused with, so slices 008–012 inherit the fix instead of each rediscovering the ambiguity.
